_note: The FACET RESOLUTION LADDER corpus (facet-contracts.md: 'a call resolves local → declared reach over the link → typed unavailable error into the ledger'). THE LAW: the caller never spells the route — the same markup ships on every surface, and where an action LIVES is a declaration, never a call site. A runtime binds ONE registered facet word (`facet` below; the kernel knows no word — it arrives as build data, and an UNBOUND runtime is the honest default). The compiled per-facet capability table (`table`) is generated from each action's `provides` (the facets whose runtime implements it LOCALLY) and `reach` (the facets that may invoke it OVER THEIR LINK — fail-closed: absent reach admits nobody, explicit `false` is the deny). The table is EXCLUSION-BLIND, exactly like the platform catalog: a row survives its module being dropped from this build, so absence can be attributed instead of guessed. THE LADDER, in order, at every runtime's ONE dispatch funnel: (1) LOCAL — a registered module answering this action wins before anything else is consulted, so a partly-local chain never pays for the table; (2) REACH — the row admits THIS facet ⇒ invoke over the link; admitted but no transport installed ⇒ the typed `unreachable`, never a hang and never a silent no-op. A generated CLIENT-LINK route (the server node's table) is the same rung and is consulted here too; (3) TYPED UNAVAILABLE — the reason IS the code (durability.md P4), four-way distinct and always through the ordinary call-failure path into the error ledger (origin 'call'), never a side channel: (a) the module IS registered here but the action is not ⇒ `unknown_action` (the caller named a wrong action — that is a caller bug, not absence); (b) the scheme exists in the product but has no implementation on this OS ⇒ `unsupported_platform` (the platform catalog, X-tier); (c) the row exists and NEITHER provides NOR reaches this facet ⇒ `unsupported_platform` — this is the NEVER-ON-THIS-FACET class, and it keeps its shipping name: durability.md P4 RETIRED the draft spelling `never_on_facet` ('never repurpose a kept name' is P5's own law, and `unsupported_platform` already meant exactly this on the wire); (d) the chain is in the build-excluded overlay ⇒ `excluded`, the DespiaExcluded entry riding verbatim as data; (e) the row PROVIDES this facet yet nothing registered ⇒ `prerequisites_missing` — the manifest promises a local implementation the runtime could not stand up (an unlinked framework, an OS floor, a dropped companion), which is a genuinely different fact from 'never here' and from 'this build dropped it'; (f) nothing known at all ⇒ `not_loaded`. PRECEDENCE is frozen by the shipped funnels and is deliberate: local > reach > unknown_action > unsupported_platform > excluded > prerequisites_missing > not_loaded. `unsupported_platform` outranks `excluded` because 'it could never answer here' is the more fundamental fact than 'this build dropped it'; `excluded` outranks `prerequisites_missing` because a build fact beats a runtime one. THE EMPTY SEAM IS NOT A FAILURE MODE: an unbound runtime (facet null) with an empty table answers exactly what the funnels answered before the ladder existed — every facet-dependent rung is skipped and (d)/(f) remain. That is what lets the ladder land in a kernel whose build has no facets yet. Case shape: `facet` = the word this runtime binds (absent/null = unbound); `local` = chain -> the actions a registered module answers HERE (absent = nothing local); `transport` = is a reach transport installed (default false); `call` = 'chain/action'; expect.rung ∈ local | reach | unavailable, and expect.code is the frozen error code for the unavailable rung (null otherwise). Runners: TS (node:test, packages/kernel) and Kotlin (:core JUnit) execute every case; Swift implements the same ladder — see the README for its lane.
